title: Computational Grammar Theory
subtitle: Structure, Operation, and the Cost of Resolution
author: Abed Kadaan
role: Computational Substrate Scientist and Principal Researcher
status: A research manuscript in progress. Not peer reviewed; proofs marked “proved here” are self-checked and await independent review.
description: A rigorous, interactive book on the formal grammars through which computational structures expose, constrain, compose and resolve their operations — and on exactly when such grammars change what computation costs.

parts.title: What Is a Computational Structure?
parts.blurb: Ordinary data structures, treated from first principles: elements, relations, operations, representations and costs — before any new notation.

parts.title: Grammar as a Computational Object
parts.blurb: The formal core: operational grammars, three semantic layers, and the admissibility languages that constrain operations.

parts.title: Classical Algorithms Reconstructed
parts.blurb: Baseline algorithms with proofs, implementations and counted costs, each mapped to its grammar — including the many cases where grammar adds nothing.

parts.title: Cost, Information, and the Limits of Grammar
parts.blurb: Preprocessing, information lower bounds, compiled operations, and what grammars cannot do to complexity classes.

parts.title: PageRank, Search, and Information Retrieval
parts.blurb: A long-form case study: the mathematics of PageRank from first principles, and what a grammatical view does and does not add.

parts.title: Modern Computational Systems
parts.blurb: Explicit models of computation graphs, retrieval, vector search and agent workflows — and careful limits on what grammar can claim about them.

parts.title: The Laboratory, the SDK, and Grammar as a Service
parts.blurb: The executable companion: how to use, extend and serve computational grammars.

parts.title: Conclusions
parts.blurb: What has actually been established, what has not, and where the research goes next.
